newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close firmer, blue chips strengthen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close firmer, blue chips strengthen.

text.p: Stocks closed firmer on Friday after fluctuating narrowly, led largely by buying of blue chips and semiconductor shares, brokers said.
But resistance remained strong at around 720, where institutions attempted to realise profits, they said.

"Abundant liquidity firmly supported the market, but selling pressure at 720 remained strong," said Choo Hee-yup, a broker at Dongwon Securities. The composite index closed 4.29 points higher at 721.00. Brokers said the Hanbo loan scandal and the defection of a high-ranking North Korean official were ignored as non-market-moving factors.
Volume totalled 39.07 million shares, compared with 49.79 shares on Thursday. Deliners outpaced gainers 433 to 370 with 111 unchanged.
Shares of semiconductor makers rose on hopes of a price recovery as a result of production cuts, brokers said.
Samsung Electronics, the world's leading memory chip maker, rose 500 won to 59,500. It briefly hit its daily high of 61,000.
LG Semicon was up 1,600 won to its daily limit-up 22,700, and Hyundai Electronics shares also climbed 2,200 won to their limit of 30,200.
Petrochemical shares also soared, backed by rising overseas demand and falling crude prices, brokers said.
Honam Petrochemical went limit-up, rising 800 won to 11,500, and Hanwha Chemical also climbed to its daily limit of 8,390, up 620 won.
Brokers said a report by the Securities Supervisory Board (SSB) on unfair stock trading caused a brief pause on the market in the afternoon. But no long-term impact was seen.
The board said it had found 17 dealers and company executives involved in insider trading and other irregularities.
